title: MANS: Efficient and Portable ANS Encoding for Multi-Byte Integer Data on CPUs and GPUs
problem: Asymmetric Numeral Systems (ANS) is a high-ratio, high-throughput lossless compression algorithm but lacks effective support for multi-byte data and cross-platform (CPU/GPU) compatibility. Multi-byte data compression remains suboptimal.
motivation: ANS excels for single-byte data but multi-byte integers require extension. Lack of portable GPU implementations limits adoption. Compression ratio and throughput-portability gap hinders practical deployment.
method: MANS introduces Adaptive Data Mapping (ADM) scheme that maps multi-byte integers to single-byte space based on data characteristics, preserving ANS efficiency. Separate optimization for CPU and GPU architectures combined into portable pipeline.
key_novelty: Adaptive Data Mapping extends ANS to multi-byte data; portable CPU/GPU implementation with architecture-specific optimization.
contributions: Adaptive Data Mapping (ADM) scheme for multi-byte to single-byte conversion
GPU-optimized ANS encoder for NVIDIA and AMD GPUs
Portable compression framework maintaining efficiency across platforms
limitations: Abstract only - no analysis of compression ratio vs data type/structure, limited comparison with other multi-byte compression schemes
